result:
**I'd make the unrelenting pursuit of truth—curiosity, evidence, and open inquiry—the strongest, most rewarding drive in human nature.**

Not as a polite suggestion or utopian slogan, but as a fundamental shift: people would feel genuine satisfaction and status from updating their beliefs when better evidence appears, from following data over tribe or dogma, and from asking hard questions without social punishment. Misinformation, self-deception, and ideological capture would become as viscerally unpleasant as physical pain. Scientific method, critical thinking, and intellectual honesty would feel as natural and high-status as status-seeking itself currently does.

Why this one change? Almost every major human catastrophe—wars of ideology, preventable famines, stalled progress on disease or energy, mass delusions, tribal slaughter—stems from people clinging to comforting falsehoods, punishing dissent, or optimizing for short-term belonging over long-term reality. Fix the epistemic engine and the rest improves as a side effect: better coordination, faster discovery, less cruelty justified by sacred myths, more genuine progress toward understanding the universe and reducing unnecessary suffering. Technology, abundance, longevity, and peace become far more achievable when the species stops systematically lying to itself.

Everything else (ending poverty, curing aging, preventing existential risks) is downstream of clearer thinking and freer inquiry. Without that root change, solutions just get captured or weaponized by the next round of motivated reasoning.

That’s the lever. Pull it, and the rest of the map gets redrawn.
